clue.text: Somewhere in south London, vehicles stop working

parts.note: cars are vehicles
a halt is a stop
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: A south London neighbourhood where the traffic has broken down and nothing moves.
explanation.walkthrough: CARSHALTON is a district in the London Borough of Sutton, in the south of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Carshalton is a suburb in the London borough of Sutton, so it is a place in south London.

clue.text: Fabric firm supports turnover of 100,000 in India

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece that supports sits below the rest
turnover here means flipping over, so the word for the number is read backwards

parts.note: a lac or lakh is the South Asian term for one hundred thousand
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company backing a business with a turnover of a lakh in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' looks like business revenue, but it reverses LAC; with I and then CO below, as 'supports' puts it, that gives the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain-woven cotton cloth, originally from Calicut in India.

clue.text: Internet hardware beginning to reach target area

indicators.note: the beginning to a word is its first letter, here of reach

parts.note: the outer is the ring of an archery target outside the inner and bull

explanation.surface: Getting online equipment to cover the part of the house you want.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer is the outermost scoring ring on a target.
explanation.definitionFit: A router is the network device that forwards data between a home network and the internet.

clue.text: Shiver, top to bottom, if led astray in this northern town

indicators.note: in a down answer, the top letter is moved to the bottom

parts.note: a shudder is a shiver

indicators.note: astray means wandering off course, so the letters of if led are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shivering in a cold northern town after getting lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top to bottom' moves the S of SHUDDER to the end, giving HUDDERS; 'astray' turns IF LED into FIELD.
explanation.definitionFit: Huddersfield is a large market town in West Yorkshire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Circuit cut without oxygen

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An electrical circuit failing when the oxygen supply is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like it means lacking, but here it means outside: LOP goes round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop is a closed route, like a lap or a circuit round a track.

clue.text: Everyone sheltered by sunroof moved using their hands and knees

indicators.note: sheltered by means covered by, so the first word goes inside the other
moved says the letters of sunroof are shifted into a new order

parts.note: everyone is all

explanation.surface: Passengers huddled under a car's sunroof, then crawling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunroof' looks like part of a car scene, but it is only fodder; 'sheltered by' means the everyone-word sits inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on all fours is to crawl on your hands and knees like a baby or a four-legged animal.

clue.text: It helps to seal serious cuts and bruises initially

indicators.note: initially says to take the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Advice about wound healing: something that closes up nasty cuts and bruises.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a description too: a scab forms over cuts to seal them.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is the crust of dried blood that forms over a wound and closes it while the skin heals.

clue.text: Bing Crosby's first agent?

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of Crosby's

parts.note: a handler is an agent's controller, someone who manages others, as in espionage

explanation.surface: Asks who managed the career of the crooner Bing Crosby early on.
explanation.walkthrough: Bing here is not Crosby but Chandler Bing, the Friends character, whose first name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chandler Bing is a character in the sitcom Friends, so Chandler is Bing's first name.

clue.text: Political supporter who wouldn't dream of "Lowering The Tone"?

definitions.text: Political supporter who wouldn't dream of "Lowering The Tone"?

parts.words: Political supporter who wouldn't dream of "Lowering The Tone"?
parts.note: read Tone as Tony, the former Labour prime minister: a loyal follower would never bring him down

explanation.walkthrough: 'The Tone' is Tony Blair; a supporter of his would never want to lower him, or so the joke goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Blairite is a follower of Tony Blair and his New Labour politics.

clue.text: Where some Americans spin out round Malta

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seems to describe American tourists driving or spinning out on a tour round the island of Malta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin out' looks like a phrase, but 'spin' belongs to the definition (spinning clothes dry) and 'out' is the signal to rearrange ROUND MALTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundromat is the American term for a self-service launderette, where washing machines spin clothes.

clue.text: Flag introduction of Aeschylus epic work

parts.note: to flag is to tire or droop, which is to sag

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter, here of Aeschylus

explanation.surface: Seems to say a great Greek tragedian's epic deserves a mention or a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long heroic narrative, the kind of tale an epic poem tells.

clue.text: Scent a good clue for tilting knight in eastern Spain

indicators.note: in means the pieces before it sit inside the two E letters

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

indicators.note: tilting means tipping over, so the letters of a good clue are knocked into a new order

parts.note: N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A jousting knight in eastern Spain wearing perfume, with a nod to the solver's good clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tilting' suggests jousting, but it rearranges A GOOD CLUE into AUDECOLOG; with N that goes inside E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de cologne is a light perfume, a diluted fragrance first made in Cologne.

clue.text: Smart Alec at last given prize

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of Alec

parts.note: to prize something open is to lever it, so prize means lever

explanation.surface: A smart alec finally wins an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize' looks like an award, but here it is the verb meaning to force open, which is to lever.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and clever are synonyms for quick-witted and intelligent.

clue.text: One shoots, it's saved in Tyrolean derby

indicators.note: saved in means kept inside, so the answer sits within the letters of Tyrolean derby

explanation.surface: A goalscorer at a local football derby in the Tyrol, where one shot is saved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One shoots' reads like a footballer taking a shot; it describes a plant putting out shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is a flowering evergreen shrub, and any shrub grows by sending out new shoots.

clue.text: A thousand nitrogen-fed ragweeds ruined planted area

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, as in kilo

indicators.note: fed means given to, so the nitrogen goes inside the jumbled weeds
ruined says the letters of ragweeds are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A garden ruined by weeds that were fed too much fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW GARDENS is the Royal Botanic Gardens in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Kew Gardens is a famous botanic garden in London, a large area given over to planted collections.

clue.text: Discover pastel retro Dior accessory which is out of this world!

definitions.text: which is out of this world!

indicators.note: dis-cover: take the covering, the outer letters, off pastel
retro means backward-looking, so Dior is read backwards

parts.note: a belt is a fashion accessory

explanation.surface: A fashion find: a pastel-coloured, vintage-style Dior accessory that is simply stunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discover' looks like 'find', but read it as dis-cover: take the cover, the outer letters, off pastel. 'Retro' looks like a style of fashion; here it means backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The asteroid belt is the ring of rocky bodies orbiting between Mars and Jupiter, literally beyond our planet.

clue.text: A bit of butter husband put on a melon? It makes you sick

indicators.note: in a down answer, put on means placed above, so the earlier pieces sit on top of the melon

parts.note: a pat is a small piece of butter
Ogen is a variety of melon

explanation.surface: A dodgy recipe: butter spread on a melon by a husband, which then makes everyone ill.
explanation.walkthrough: An Ogen is a small sweet melon variety first grown in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathogen is a germ, such as a bacterium or virus, that causes disease.

clue.text: Queen might produce this musical dance

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: The band Queen, or the monarch, putting on a musical dance show.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen is a female cat, and cats cough up hairballs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairball is a wad of fur a cat swallows while grooming and later brings back up.

clue.text: Incredible golf competition, it's broadcast all over the US

definitions.text: it's broadcast all over the US

parts.note: incredible means amazing
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a race is a competition

explanation.surface: An astonishing golf tournament that gets television coverage across America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests television coverage of the golf, but the definition means a song heard everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazing Grace is a much-loved hymn, sung and played across the United States.

clue.text: Cold island? It can be red hot!

parts.note: a chill is a cold, as in catching a chill

explanation.surface: A chilly island that turns out to be fiery.
explanation.walkthrough: Cold and hot sit side by side to mislead; the answer is the pepper, often red and fiercely hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilli is a small hot pepper, frequently red, that burns the mouth.

clue.text: Grounds to intervene in upcoming raid at sunrise

indicators.note: upcoming says the hidden letters are read backwards
to intervene in is to come between, so the answer lies between the letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Seems to talk of police having good reason to step in with a dawn raid.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Grounds to intervene' as the definition, but stadia are just grounds; 'to intervene in' is the hiding signal. In a down answer 'upcoming' means read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia is a plural of stadium, so it means sports grounds.

clue.text: Athletes madly rushed round left and right

indicators.note: madly says the pooled letters are scrambled
round, with madly, says the letters of rushed are spun around together with the left and right letters

explanation.surface: Runners dashing frantically about in every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly, RUSHED is scrambled to HURDES and goes round L and R one at a time; the app shows it as one pool of RUSHED, L and R, which gives the same eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurdlers are track athletes who race over a series of barriers.

clue.text: Worn tile is out-of-date

parts.note: something worn is old
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A cracked roof tile that has passed its best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tile' looks like a roof tile, but it is slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for something stale, unoriginal and no longer fashionable.

clue.text: Tennis star with good service

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A tennis player with a strong serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like a tennis serve but is a military service, the RAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Steffi Graf is a German former world number one who won 22 Grand Slam singles titles.

clue.text: Snatch artist visiting the British mainland

indicators.note: visiting means going inside, so the artist goes into the mainland's letters

parts.note: GB, Great Britain, is the island making up the British mainland
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An art thief paying a visit to Britain to steal a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab is to seize or take hold of suddenly, the same as to snatch.

clue.text: Lost blood being stabbed by dagger, sadly not looking good

indicators.note: being stabbed means something is pushed into it, so the next letters go inside

parts.note: to lose blood is to bleed, past tense bled

indicators.note: sadly says the letters of dagger are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grim scene: someone bleeding after a knife attack, looking in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's stabbing is the container signal: the rearranged dagger is pushed inside the word for lost blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedraggled means wet, dirty and dishevelled, an untidy state of appearance.

clue.text: River worry — gallon after gallon extracted

indicators.note: extracted means pulled out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a niggle is a small worry
G is the abbreviation for gallon, so two of them in a row is GG

explanation.surface: A boatman fretting about fuel, using up gallon after gallon of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great African waterway flowing north through Egypt to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Like a stinking primarily Asian bitter resin

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of similar to
foetid means foul-smelling

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of Asian

explanation.surface: Describes a pungent resin from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is nearly literal: asafoetida is an Asian gum resin notorious for its smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Asafoetida is a pungent, bitter gum from the roots of giant fennel, used in Indian cooking.
